correctness.rationale: The marked Poisson process gives independent fair source bits. The two strict confidence boundaries form an irreversible exit set; geometrically probable constant runs force almost-sure exit, with symmetry giving equal polarization probabilities. Exact binary expansions prove the first (m-1)-bit early exit and later m-run criterion. The fair run-length recurrence yields E[N_m]=2^m-3, and the independent exponential waiting times give E[T_m]. The all-active regime has an invariant uniform law but fails a.s. path convergence. Exact finite-state checks support, but do not replace, the all-m proof.

limitations: Only equal-rate Poisson source clocks, directed one-sided updates, strictly centered flexible opinion, symmetric fixed endpoints, and halfway compromise.
No generalization to arbitrary graphs/non-exponential time distributions; uniform stationary law is acknowledged prior knowledge.
No independent external audit has been performed.

value.rationale: The exact first-loss time is a natural observable of competing influence, with a sharp critical divergence. At the minimally nontrivial graph size it distinguishes almost-sure eventual polarization from statistically stationary persistent fluctuation. Dyadic parameter choices are forced by the binary halving dynamics; the explicit infinite family and inverse-gap growth are not arbitrary numerology or a finite experiment.
